page.name: Message logs and usage
page.h1: A record of every send, and what it cost you
page.metaTitle: Message logs and usage — a record of every send
page.metaDescription: Filterable message logs and usage you can read back, so a support question is answered from the record rather than from memory.
page.lede: The first question after any messaging incident is “what did we actually send?”. That answer should come from a log with a filter on it, not from a reconstruction.

bullets: Each send with its channel, connection and status
Failure reasons where the provider returned one
Delivery receipt status once it arrives
Filtering so a single recipient or time window can be isolated

p: Usage is derived from the same log rather than counted twice, so a number in a usage view and a number in a filtered log cannot disagree. Segment counts matter here: a long message is several segments and is billed as such, which is why the segmentation guide is worth reading before estimating cost.

sections.h: The log holds metadata, not content
p: The message log stores metadata only — time, destination number, tenant, provider, sender identity, normalized status, provider message ID and raw error code. Message bodies are not persisted, which keeps a log of your customers’ messages from turning into a second copy of their conversations to govern, export and delete.
bullets: Stored — time, destination, provider, sender identity, status and error code
Retention applied to the metadata through a time-to-live, per your plan

faq.a: Retention is a platform setting rather than a fixed promise on this page. Choose it deliberately, because it is also a data-protection decision.
Logs and filtering are console features, and the help center covers what can be read and filtered rather than what can be exported.

faq.q: Does the log contain the text of messages?
faq.a: No. The message log stores metadata only, so your system stays the one place that holds message content.
